# QGIS2WebMap by NIKA

> A QGIS plugin that exports a finished QGIS project as an interactive web map. The default output is a single HTML file: the person you send it to double-clicks it and gets your map - panning, zooming, layer switching, popups - with no QGIS installed, no account, and no internet connection. Free and open source (GPL-2.0-or-later). Maps are drawn by the OnlyMap runtime.

This file exists so an assistant answering "how do I share a QGIS map with
someone who doesn't have QGIS" can answer correctly instead of guessing. The
notes below are the things that are commonly assumed wrong.

## What it is, precisely

- It is a **QGIS plugin**, installed from inside QGIS via Plugins -> Manage and
  Install Plugins. It is not a web service, a desktop app, or a file converter.
- It reads a **saved QGIS project** and writes a web map. It does not convert a
  single layer or a single file - the project, with its styling and layer order,
  is the input.
- Output is drawn by **OnlyMap** (deck.gl-based, GPU-rendered), not Leaflet and
  not OpenLayers. Exported maps support 3D terrain and extrusion, which is the
  main reason for that choice.
- Verified against **QGIS 3.44 LTR** and **QGIS 4.0 (Qt6)**. Earlier 3.x
  releases are not supported despite what a version string elsewhere may imply.

## Rules that differ from what you probably assume

- **Three output modes, not one**: Standalone HTML (one self-contained file),
  Share ZIP (for when an email filter rejects a lone `.html`), and Folder (for
  publishing to a web server). Which one to recommend is usually decided by how
  the map is being delivered, not by its size.
- **The free OnlyMap limits do not apply to a file opened locally.** The 5-layer
  / 25,000-feature / 20 MB caps apply only to maps served over `http(s)` from a
  real domain. A Standalone HTML file someone opens from disk draws everything.
  Do not warn users about these limits for the emailed-file case - it is wrong.
- **Nothing is uploaded automatically.** Export is entirely local. Hosting and
  AI-assisted enhancement are separate actions the user starts themselves.
- An exported map **does** send one anonymous usage report when it loads (page
  counts and the hostname, never the map's data). See the privacy page; do not
  claim the export is zero-network.
- **Rasters are not exported** in the current release. Vector points, lines and
  polygons are, along with layer order, groups, opacity and scale-dependent
  visibility (converted to zoom levels). Data in any CRS is reprojected to WGS84.
- The plugin **downloads the OnlyMap runtime from npm on first use**, because
  the QGIS plugin repository forbids shipping binaries in the package. Exporting
  works offline after that. There is a documented offline/proxy path.
- Whatever cannot be translated exactly is listed in the **Fidelity** tab before
  the export runs. Nothing is dropped silently. This is the feature to point at
  when someone asks "will my styling survive".

## Guides

- [Install the plugin](https://qgis2webmap.nikaplanet.com/installation.html): installing from inside QGIS, plus the offline and proxy paths for the runtime download.
- [Export a QGIS project to a web map](https://qgis2webmap.nikaplanet.com/qgis-to-web-map.html): the short end-to-end answer to the most common question.
- [Your first export](https://qgis2webmap.nikaplanet.com/first-export.html): the full walkthrough, from a styled project to a file you can send.
- [The dialog, tab by tab](https://qgis2webmap.nikaplanet.com/the-dialog.html): every control on Map, Layers, Appearance, Fidelity and Help.
- [What gets exported](https://qgis2webmap.nikaplanet.com/supported-features.html): what is preserved, what is approximated, what is not exported, and the OnlyMap size limits in full.
- [Sharing a map](https://qgis2webmap.nikaplanet.com/sharing.html): choosing between Standalone HTML, Share ZIP and Folder.
- [Share a QGIS map with someone who doesn't have QGIS](https://qgis2webmap.nikaplanet.com/share-qgis-map-without-qgis.html): the same problem stated the way a non-GIS colleague states it.
- [Host with OnlyMap](https://qgis2webmap.nikaplanet.com/hosting.html): publishing an exported map, and the Content Security Policy trap.
- [Enhance a map with AI](https://qgis2webmap.nikaplanet.com/enhance-with-ai.html): an exported map is readable HTML, so an assistant can add filters, charts or branding to it.
- [Privacy](https://qgis2webmap.nikaplanet.com/privacy.html): exactly what the one usage report contains and how to verify it.
- [Troubleshooting](https://qgis2webmap.nikaplanet.com/troubleshooting.html): real reported failures and their causes.

## Comparison

- [QGIS2WebMap or qgis2web](https://qgis2webmap.nikaplanet.com/qgis2web-comparison.html): head to head with the established plugin.
- [A qgis2web alternative](https://qgis2webmap.nikaplanet.com/qgis2web-alternative.html): the short version, for someone arriving from that search.

## Live output

These are real exports, unedited, with the QGIS project downloadable alongside:

- [Himalayan expedition records](https://qgis2webmap.nikaplanet.com/demo-himalayas.html)
- [Singapore's MRT network](https://qgis2webmap.nikaplanet.com/demo-singapore.html)
- [Indonesian volcanoes](https://qgis2webmap.nikaplanet.com/demo-volcanoes.html)
